title: The Serpent’s Breath: Escape from Chichén Itzá
description: A 30-minute digital escape room where a Latin American archaeologist must translate carved symbols, solve physics puzzles, manage oxygen, and escape a sealed temple chamber before the usable air runs out.

answerKey.method: Escape route unlocked by translating carvings and applying physics: light/shadow, balance, airflow, echo timing, and astronomy alignment.
answerKey.motive: The temple was built as a trial of knowledge: only someone who respects the writings, sculptures, and laws of nature can leave safely.
answerKey.keyEvidence: The serpent glyph warns that fire reveals truth but steals breath; airflow and echo clues point away from dead-end tunnels; the final star-serpent alignment opens the oxygen gate.
answerKey.explanation: The fastest safe escape is to use the torch in short bursts, translate the serpent warnings, follow the tunnel with moving air and the shortest echo delay, balance the jade weights, then align the feathered-serpent shadow with the ceiling star carving.

openingNarration: You are Dr. Reyes, a Latin American archaeologist called to Chichén Itzá after ground-penetrating scans revealed a sealed chamber beneath the old stone complex. For years you studied how Mayan builders used sculpture, astronomy, mathematics, and writing to preserve knowledge. Tonight, the temple answers back. A stone door drops behind you. Your oxygen monitor flashes: 30 minutes of usable air. A torch rests beside the entry. It can reveal hidden carvings, but every second of flame burns oxygen faster. The walls, floor, and ceiling are covered in ancient symbols. They are not decoration. They are instructions. Translate them, trust the physics, choose the correct paths, and escape before the Serpent’s Breath runs out.
revealScript: Temple run complete. The Serpent’s Breath tested oxygen discipline, translation, and physics. The safe route required short torch bursts, careful reading of carvings, airflow awareness, echo timing, balanced weights, and the final serpent-shadow alignment. Those who escaped fastest used knowledge without wasting breath.

publicClues.title: Oxygen Warning
publicClues.text: Your wrist monitor reads 30:00. The chamber air is usable, but limited. Flame consumes oxygen faster than calm breathing.
publicClues.timelineNote: Timer begins when the temple seals.

publicClues.title: The First Carving
publicClues.text: A serpent glyph curls around a flame. Beneath it: 'Light shows the road. Hunger of fire steals the sky from the lungs.'
publicClues.timelineNote: Torchlight reveals hidden pigment in the stone.

publicClues.title: Three Tunnel Mouths
publicClues.text: The left tunnel is still and dusty. The center tunnel returns a short echo. The right tunnel carries a faint moving draft across your cheek.

publicClues.title: Balance Room
publicClues.text: Three carved stones show jaguar, maize, and jade. A floor scale sinks unevenly unless the weights follow the carved ratio.
publicClues.timelineNote: The temple uses mass and balance to test entry.

publicClues.title: Ceiling Map
publicClues.text: On the ceiling, stars surround a serpent head. The shadow of a raised torch can connect the serpent eye to the morning-star mark.
publicClues.timelineNote: Torch angle matters more than torch duration.

publicClues.title: Final Oxygen Gate
publicClues.text: The exit seal has three symbols: Breath, Shadow, and Current. The carvings repeat one warning: 'Do not choose the quiet mouth.'

casefeed.title: Entry Log
casefeed.text: Dr. Reyes enters the hidden chamber beneath Chichén Itzá. The stone door seals. The oxygen timer starts at 30:00.

casefeed.title: Translation Note
casefeed.text: Mayan inscriptions often combine image, sound, and meaning. Read sculpture placement, not just symbols.

casefeed.title: Temple Physics Warning
casefeed.text: The chamber is designed around light, air, weight, and echo. Wrong turns waste oxygen; careful observation saves it.

phone.title: Oxygen Monitor
phone.text: O₂ Reserve: 30 minutes estimated. Torch flame detected: oxygen burn rate increases while active.

phone.title: Sensor Flicker
phone.text: Air current detected from the east-facing passage. Still air detected from the north passage.

messages.title: Field Team Message
messages.text: Comms are weak. Remember: Chichén Itzá builders aligned structures with sky events. Check walls and ceilings together.

messages.title: Final Warning From Surface
messages.text: Your oxygen telemetry is dropping. Use the torch only when reading carvings or casting alignment shadows.

maps.title: Temple Sketch
maps.text: Chamber layout: Descent Hall → Shadow Wall → Balance Room → Three Paths → Oxygen Gate.

maps.title: Path Choice
maps.text: Draft moves toward the southeast tunnel. The quiet north tunnel has no dust disturbance and no oxygen movement.

photos.title: Torch-Revealed Pigment
photos.text: A faded blue-green pigment appears only in torchlight, forming a serpent body pointing toward a wall niche.

photos.title: Serpent Shadow
photos.text: When the torch is low, the serpent head shadow misses the ceiling star. When raised to shoulder height, the eye nearly aligns.

contacts.title: Mentor Note: Dr. Itzel Cocom
contacts.text: The writing is a system. Floor carvings often mark danger, wall carvings give instruction, ceiling carvings reveal timing or alignment.

notes.title: Symbol Glossary Fragment
notes.text: Breath = moving air. Serpent = path or test. Flame = revealed truth and consumed oxygen. Closed eye = dead end.

notes.title: Balance Ratio
notes.text: Jade appears twice, maize once, jaguar three times. The floor scale expects a 2:1:3 relationship.

files.title: Physics Field Sheet
files.text: Echo timing clue: shorter echo usually means a shorter chamber or blocked path; moving air suggests connection to an opening or vent.

files.title: Lever Notes
files.text: A balanced lever has equal torque on both sides: force multiplied by distance. Heavier stones can balance lighter stones placed farther away.

browser.title: Chichén Itzá Research Cache
browser.text: The site is associated with astronomy, architecture, carved serpent imagery, and ceremonial movement through space.

browser.title: Shadow Alignment Reminder
browser.text: A shadow can act like a pointer. Move the light source, not the wall, to change the shadow angle.

rounds.title: Chamber 1: The Sealed Descent
rounds.objective: Understand the oxygen danger and learn the torch tradeoff.
rounds.dialogue: The door seals. Oxygen is now the real clock.
rounds.countdownReview: The torch reveals hidden writing, but fire costs breath.

rounds.title: Chamber 2: The Shadow Wall
rounds.objective: Use light and shadow to find the first safe direction.
rounds.dialogue: The carvings only speak when flame touches stone.
rounds.countdownReview: Look for meaning in the shadow, not only the symbol.

rounds.title: Chamber 3: The Balance Room
rounds.objective: Solve the lever and weight puzzle using ratios and torque.
rounds.dialogue: The floor listens to mass, distance, and balance.
rounds.countdownReview: The wrong weight order wastes oxygen.

rounds.title: Chamber 4: The Three Paths
rounds.objective: Choose the tunnel using airflow, echo, and carvings.
rounds.dialogue: Not every open mouth leads to life.
rounds.countdownReview: The quiet tunnel is the most dangerous.

rounds.title: Chamber 5: The Oxygen Gate
rounds.objective: Combine translations and physics for the final seal.
rounds.dialogue: Breath, shadow, and current must agree.
rounds.countdownReview: Raise the torch only long enough to align the serpent eye.

rounds.title: Final Escape
rounds.objective: Submit the escape sequence before the oxygen lock closes.
rounds.dialogue: Choose the final route. The temple will not wait.

questions.prompt: The torch reveals hidden carvings, but what is the survival tradeoff?

options.label: It helps reveal clues while burning oxygen faster.
It stops the oxygen timer completely.
It should stay on for the whole game.
It only affects score, not survival.

questions.prompt: A serpent shadow points away from the obvious doorway. What should the archaeologist trust?

options.label: The largest doorway, because it is easiest to see.
The shadow alignment created by the torch and carving.
The quietest passage with no airflow.
The path with the most dust.

questions.prompt: The balance room shows jade:maize:jaguar as 2:1:3. Which action fits the carving?

options.label: Place all stones equally on the scale.
Ignore the ratio and choose the heaviest stone.
Balance the stones using the 2:1:3 relationship.
Keep adding weight until the floor breaks.

questions.prompt: Three tunnels appear. Which clue best points toward a survivable escape route?

options.label: The tunnel with completely still air.
The tunnel marked with the closed-eye glyph.
The tunnel with the longest, deepest echo.
The tunnel with moving airflow and matching serpent glyphs.

questions.prompt: The final gate shows Breath, Shadow, and Current. What is the correct escape principle?

options.label: Use moving air, brief torchlight, and the serpent-shadow alignment together.
Use the torch continuously until every wall is bright.
Choose the quiet mouth because it feels safer.
Ignore the ceiling carvings and follow the floor only.

questions.prompt: What is the safest final route out of the temple?

options.label: North tunnel, closed-eye glyph, no airflow.
Left tunnel, deepest echo, heavy dust.
Southeast airflow tunnel after aligning the serpent eye shadow.
Any tunnel after turning the torch off forever.

questions.prompt: What does the phrase 'The Serpent’s Breath' mean in the escape?

options.label: A monster in the chamber.
The limited moving air that reveals the living path before oxygen runs out.
A code telling players to run randomly.
A warning to never use light.

questions.prompt: Which player strategy earns the fastest escape?

options.label: Keep the torch on and inspect every stone slowly.
Choose paths quickly without reading carvings.
Use every hint immediately.
Use short torch bursts, translate key symbols, and trust physics clues.
